title: Visual Job
description: The compiled visual job record (AES-V2.7 / SUE-565). The durable knowledge is the semantic/artifact/reference/brand profile state; the compiled prompt is an output of that state, not the source of truth. This record carries the full lineage so a bad result routes back to the layer that produced it (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5). See schemas/VISUAL-JOB-CONTRACT.md.

intent_ref.description: Editorial Intent this job traces to (schemas/editorial-intent.schema.json intent_id).

calibration_ref.description: The calibration version active when this job was compiled (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §6, §10 AES-V2.10). Nullable because calibration versioning may not yet be active; recorded explicitly either way so a later verdict is attributed to the calibration that produced it, not whichever is current.

package_ref.description: Editorial Package reference, when this job is planned from a package rather than a single article. Exactly one of article_ref/package_ref must be present — checked by scripts/compile-visual-prompt.mjs, not by this schema.

artifact_profile.description: A visual artifact profile id from the artifact axis (editorial/profiles/axes.json, editorial/profiles/artifact/visual-*.json). The vocabulary is owned by that directory, not this enum (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §8 extension rule) — real membership is enforced by scripts/lib/visual-job-core.mjs's UNKNOWN_PROFILE check against the directory, not by this pattern alone.

article_title.description: Article-title lineage and verification input for generative/hybrid jobs. Core's recognisable-form prompt check catches honest inclusion, not deliberate obfuscation; it is not a security control. The compiler never reads this value, and rendered-image title detection belongs to vision review.

visual_brief.description: SUE-642 durable VisualBrief. Required by core for generative/hybrid routes; optional for legacy deterministic evidence jobs.

render_spec.description: SUE-642 durable RenderSpec. Required by core for generative/hybrid routes; optional for legacy deterministic evidence jobs.

renderer.description: Full runtime lineage for the renderer layer (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5 'renderer' routing layer). Model/provider drift is an editorial quality event even when semantic_spec, artifact_profile, audience, reference traits, and brand_profile are unchanged: recording runtime identity here — never inside compiled_prompt — is what lets a quality regression route to this layer instead of being misattributed to brand_profile or semantic_spec.

compiled_prompt.description: Deterministic string assembly from the declared inputs only. Absent when information_gain.verdict is skip.

compiled_from.description: Every input the compiled_prompt was assembled from. Required whenever compiled_prompt is present.

compiled_prompt_adapter.description: Prompt-dialect lineage only. It may change the disposable compiled prompt but never the VisualBrief, RenderSpec, reference authority, or renderer runtime identity.

brand_conflicts.description: Human-visible evidence of a RenderSpec requirement that exceeds the current brand default. This is not approval, publication authority, or a lock.

requires_owner_gate.description: Derived owner-gate routing flag. Core requires true exactly when brand_conflicts is non-empty; this is not approval, a lock, or publication authority.

approved_asset.description: The human-approval lock (SUE-639 / editorial/APPROVED-VISUAL-ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md §2). Absent while the job is still producing candidates. Present with state human_approved_locked, it makes approval machine state rather than conversational memory: the approved pixels/vectors become the authority for visual identity, and the normal edge back to a generative renderer is closed. Identity completeness for a locked asset is enforced by scripts/lib/visual-job-core.mjs, not by this schema alone, so a lock claimed without a digest or geometry fails rather than validating hollow.

revision.description: How a post-approval request was classified (editorial/APPROVED-VISUAL-ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md §3). Only meaningful alongside approved_asset — a revision intent without an approved asset is rejected, so there is exactly one authority for post-approval routing.

visual_production.description: Optional SUE-645/SUE-648 declared production control state. It does not approve, lock, publish, render, or observe a provider.

approved_asset.description: Approval lock record. state is the only schema-required field: candidate carries no master identity yet, and the identity requirements for human_approved_locked are cross-field checks in scripts/lib/visual-job-core.mjs (a raster master needs pixel geometry, a vector master a view_box).

state.description: candidate: still a rendered candidate, generation remains open. human_approved_locked: a human accepted this exact artifact; it is now an immutable master.

master_ref.description: Reference to the approved artifact itself — repository path, blob ref, or asset id. Never a conversational description of it.

master_digest.description: Content digest of the approved master, so a later derivative can prove same-master lineage.

approval_context.description: Which article/package/version the approval was given against.

renderer_lineage.description: The runtime that produced the approved master, when it was generated. This is where a generative origin stays auditable after the lock closes the generative route on the job itself: renderer_route on a locked, non-semantic job describes the post-approval derivative route, not how the master was first drawn.

native_geometry.description: Native geometry of the approved master: width/height for a raster master, view_box for a vector one. Which of the two is required is decided by approved_asset.format in scripts/lib/visual-job-core.mjs.

revision.description: Post-approval revision intent and its identity flags (editorial/APPROVED-VISUAL-ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md §3). publication_only/fidelity_only/format_only/layout_only are derivative/media work and may never reach a generative renderer; local_edit and concept_change reopen generation only with explicit authorization.

request.description: The human request this intent classifies, recorded verbatim so a misclassification is reviewable ('make it high quality' is fidelity_only, not concept_change).

revision_authorization.description: Explicit human authority to reopen the renderer. Required for local_edit (with a bounded delta and the invariants it must not touch) and for concept_change (an explicit request for a different image).

statement.description: What the human actually asked for, in their words.

bounded_delta.description: For local_edit: exactly what may change. An empty or absent delta is not a bounded edit.

protected_invariants.description: For local_edit: composition, text, values, colours, and subject identity that must survive the edit unchanged.

runtime.description: Renderer-layer lineage. tool/tool_version identify the rendering pipeline (e.g. a deterministic SVG compiler); provider/model/model_version identify the underlying generative runtime where one is used. Deterministic tools still record provider/model as the tool's own identity so the field is never blank. None of this may appear inside compiled_prompt — see context_isolation.

model_version.description: Exact model version or a dated model alias, so quality drift from a silent model swap is diagnosable.

quality_tier.description: Reasoning/quality tier, where the provider exposes one. Absent for tools with no such tier.

traits_applied.description: Which concrete audience adjustments were actually applied to this job, not the whole profile.

semantic_spec.description: What the image must communicate — the information, not the styling.

information_gain.description: Gate 1 (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §8; editorial/VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md). Cheap semantic preflight before any rendering. skip is a first-class, non-failing outcome.

verdict.description: proceed: the visual earns its place. skip: correctly deciding not to make the image — not an error.

density_check.description: Gate 2 (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §8; editorial/SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md; editorial/SUENGJ-INFOGRAPHIC-CALIBRATION.md §2). The compiled job's semantic and visual density must match its artifact profile.

match.description: false means the job FAILS (e.g. a body infographic compiled at thumbnail density).

selected_reference_traits.description: Traits only, never a reference body (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §2).

authoritative_override.description: A reference trait listed here is the only way a reference may outrank the brand default, per editorial/profiles/brand/suengj-com.v1.json priority_rule.

context_isolation.description: Required allowlist, not optional. Models the fix for SUE-531 (built-in generative image attempts leaked unrelated recent project/conversation context into dashboard artwork).

excluded.description: Assertion that these categories were excluded from the compiled prompt. renderer_runtime_identity covers provider/model/model_version/quality_tier: that identity is lineage, not an input, and must never reach compiled_prompt text.
